hook: Set aside a long evening: this is a novella-length file built from recovered logs, exploration transcripts and a run of debriefings. A ruined complex has turned up in a Texas state park bearing the markings of Site-13, a site the Foundation's own records say was never built, and the title asks the obvious question. Expect a lot of body horror on the way down; the article does not look away from what happens to the people who go in.
whyItMatters:
1730 combines two things the wiki does well, the doomed exploration log and the alternate-history Foundation, and lets each feed the other. The first half is a dungeon crawl that keeps killing its teams; the second half is a rescue mission whose survivors explain, piece by piece, what the Foundation of their world became.

It also gives large roles to Mobile Task Force Tau-5 "Samsara" and to Bobble the Clown, both tagged on the page, so readers who know those names will find them doing a lot of work here.
thingsToNotice:
The early teams die in ways that set the rules of the place: leech-like creatures crawl down throats and wear the bodies, people with fire burning from their ears explode at any sound, symbols on the walls spread the same effect to anyone who sees them, and the halls rearrange themselves. Meanwhile the recovered files show the rot from inside: an ethics chair who is also head of the GOC ethics board explaining why humanoid anomalies have no rights, test logs on a reality-bender revived between tortures, and orders to empty the humanoid wing into the body pit.

The answer comes in layers. Hadley's letter to Director Emerson admits she caused the breach by sparing Elijah, a blood-drinking toddler-minded boy sent to be burned, and dares Emerson to fire the Thresher. Scott's debrief fills in the rest: funding cuts, a GOC takeover, an Ethics chair shot for objecting, vivisections, even the Abrahamic God placed in containment, and Hadley stripped and beaten in a corridor before her revenge. In the rescue, the eerily calm Tau-5 operatives, who are killed and still sit for their debriefs, work beside the broken human squads, and Captain Hollis, who vanished at the Thresher in the first act, walks back to it after a vision she never describes and fires it, laughing and weeping, leaving a 1km crater where Site-13 stood.
